1.why: Only option punctuating 'nevertheless' as a conjunctive adverb between two clauses (semicolon before, comma after).

2.why: The set is bare-verb vs three punctuation marks; no mark belongs between a subject and its verb.

3.why: Apostrophe ladder with one impossible form ('students's'); plural possessive is the standard key in a four-way possessive set.

4.why: Modifier item: 'the ancient elm tree' is the concrete noun the participial opener would describe, and C/D are the classic non-fixing rewrites.

5.why: Three plural forms (were/are/have) against one singular 'has' - the odd form out is the key.

6.why: 'Painted more than five centuries ago' is an introductory participial phrase, so a comma before the main clause.

7.why: Subject is 'The array', singular, so the singular present 'generates'.

8.why: Tense ladder whose only sequence-of-tenses form is the past perfect 'had removed'.

9.why: 'There ___ numerous inconsistencies' takes a plural verb, and the past 'were' matches 'had to correct'.

10.why: Single comma closing a modifier before the following clause; D double-commas and C would need two independent clauses.

11.why: Semicolon is the only option that can join 'efficient' clause to the independent 'trains arrive' clause.

12.why: Three options repeat 'on the length of the nights'; 'than' completes the comparative correlative that the set is built around.

13.why: Possessive/contraction quartet; the singular possessive 'its' is the standard key against the homophone traps.

14.why: Agreement set with one non-finite ('continuing') and one odd past perfect; singular present 'continues' is the fitted form.

15.why: Three plural forms against the single singular 'was' - the singular is the outlier and the key.

16.why: Singular 'has' against plural 'have'/'had' and the conditional 'would have'.

17.why: Dangling-modifier fix: only 'applicants must submit' supplies a human agent as subject; the other three are agentless.

18.why: Singular present 'strikes' against two plural forms and a past progressive.

19.why: Final list element after an introduction; the colon is the only option that introduces a list rather than merely joining.

20.why: Parallelism with 'to analyze' and 'to draft' requires the infinitive 'to present'.

21.why: Pronoun set splits singular ('its own', 'his own') from plural; 'its own' is the neutral singular possessive key.

22.why: 'failure, being' is a giveaway wrong; the colon is the option that can introduce an explanation that need not be an independent clause.

23.why: 'the comet, ___ orbit spans...' needs the possessive relative 'whose'.

24.why: Singular present 'grows' against two plural forms and a non-finite participle.
